  "text": "The voices belonged to two fishermen and the constable, drawn uphill by the harbor bells. Elias handed over the ledger before the harbor master could speak. When the constable opened it, a loose page slipped free. It bore a sketch of the reef and a line of figures beneath his brother’s name.

“They paid for the light,” Mara said.

The harbor master lowered his eyes. The constable took the matches from him and led him down the path. Elias watched until their lanterns disappeared among the warehouses.

Mara remained beside him. “There’s something else in the photograph,” she said. From her coat she drew a small, rain-softened print of three men standing outside the customs house. Elias recognized his brother at once. On the back, in his familiar hand, were two words: Ask Ada.

Ada had tended the lighthouse before its lantern went dark. Elias had assumed she knew nothing about the wreck; for years she had said little to anyone. Mara folded the photograph and offered it to him.

At dawn they found Ada at her kitchen table, trimming a wick for an oil lamp. She studied the photograph without surprise. Then she opened a drawer and brought out a sealed envelope.

“He left this with me the morning he sailed,” she said. “I was afraid to give it to you after he was gone.”

Elias held the envelope but did not open it yet. Through Ada’s window he could see the lighthouse across the harbor. Its lantern room was empty, and the stairs would need repair. He asked whether she still had the key."
